Michael Oluwafemi: The top of the draft board could belong to a receiver. Washington’s Oluwafemi brings generational potential, elite deep-ball ability and the athleticism to rise above defenders. Another standout season could make him the rare wideout with a legitimate case to go first overall.
Kareem Carter: There may not be much room to operate when Carter is tracking the play. USC’s linebacker covers ground in a hurry and has the athleticism to stay with elusive offensive players in space. That rare range gives him an early case for a high selection.
DaQuan Battles: Contact is where Battles starts making his case. Ohio State’s powerful back can keep a rushing attack moving by creating yards after defenders reach him, giving an offense an identity on the ground. His early projection puts even a top-five selection in play.
Zaquan Newton: A defensive front can build around a player like Newton. Georgia’s interior lineman offers the strength to anchor and the presence to control space in the middle, giving him an early projection as a potential star when his college days are finished.
Quentin Sosa: Running directly at Sosa is a risky proposition. The Ohio State interior defender excels at the point of attack and can shut down rushing lanes before they develop. His strength also offers intriguing pass-rush potential as he prepares for another season.
Jaiden Bloodworth: A 6-foot-6 lineman isn’t supposed to get upfield this quickly. Alabama’s Bloodworth brings movement skills and a substantial frame to the offensive line, giving coaches the flexibility to envision him at multiple spots. His versatility makes him a compelling early prospect.
Azizi Akpabio: Receivers have to earn their space against Akpabio. Arizona’s big, physical corner excels pressing at the line and adds tackling ability to the run defense, giving the secondary a presence who can affect the game before and after a throw.
Will Hoggard: When Hoggard gets going, Stanford’s passing game can gather momentum in a hurry. The quarterback has flashed stretches that put his upside on display, making his upcoming season an opportunity to build on those high points and strengthen his early draft case.
Rontay Jenkins: Jenkins arrives at Tennessee with an arm that can make scouts stop and watch. After producing at Georgia Tech, the quarterback gets a new stage for his elite throwing talent, and evaluators will be watching for another step forward this season.
Zion Ellis: Ellis lets the opening develop before showing why defenses have to account for him. Georgia’s back combines patience and vision with the talent to enter top-ten conversations, giving scouts an intriguing runner to follow as the new season unfolds.
